target_claim: Processing the explicitly constructed family Gn (complete DAG on v0..vn-1, w(vi,vj) = -2^i) with Dijkstra's algorithm requires at least 2^n - 1 Relax invocations, i.e. Omega(2^n) relaxation steps.
source_quote:
Therefore, processing Gn requires at least 2n −1 relaxations, proving that
Dijkstra’s algorithm performs Ω(2n) relaxation steps in the worst case even for
DAGs with negative edge weights.
test_sketch: Build Gn exactly as specified (vertices v0..vn-1, edges (vi,vj) for i<j, weight -2^i) and run Dijkstra with lazy re-insertion (the variant the solution's own trace describes), instrumenting a counter on every Relax call. For n = 2..12 the counter reads n(n-1)/2 (1, 3, 6, ..., 66), while the claimed lower bound 2^n - 1 is 3, 7, ..., 4095 - the measured operation count falls polynomially short of the claimed exponential lower bound at every n >= 2. The induction is wrong because each vertex's tentative distance is improved only along one chain (weights depend only on the source index), so subgraphs are not re-processed exponentially often.
